Its an indie masterpiece. Music and story are awesome and the gameplay is very short and satisfying. Took me 8 hours to complete the game yet it feels like 80. 
Balancing was very good and it was not very difficult which makes it super fun for employed people.
Its worth your money and if you are a fan of solemn and somber settings this game is definitely for you.
Combat and spell variety is consistent and I have found every spell and weapon to be reasonably powerful.
It runs well on all platforms and has pixel art style which gives enormous performance boost.
Highly recommend 9/10!

Game was fun till I was out exploring and discovering stuff on the surface. Then it started to force me to enter the caves, which had important equipment that required too much back-tracking to get them. The slow climbing and walking speeds, with ever increasing attacks to my base this game felt stuck between a metroidvania and a open world survival-crafter. 

Also, turns out the 'story' and most of the 'mysteries' in the world are there just for the rule of cool and to draw gasps from the player over having anything with much meaning. Which makes the forced exploration useless. Not the game I was assuming it to be, so I will not recommend unless you tweak some specific systems in the game with cheats.
It may still need some optimizing, but damn was this fun....
I like the game just don't like the energy bar or the fact that the days go by so fast. Other than those two things of my personal opinion it is an ok game.

Animal Well is a fantastic 2D adventure platformer that was made great attention and care. Movement feels very good, puzzles and challenges are paced well, and I was regularly surprised and delighted by what I found as I progressed. Near the end, I did consult an online guide regarding where to bring a certain object to, but this was ultimately because I did not put available information together myself. 

It took me about 20 hours to beat* Animal Well. I played on Steam Deck with my new 2026 Steam Controller. The game ran beautifully without issue.

*By "beat" I mean seeing the game credits via what I understand to be the "normal path." The guide I read references substantial "post-credits" content that I have not seen.

It pains me to say that this game is just a joyless cash grab.  I appreciate how much was pulled from the film, but it just does not get the job done, especially for this price.

Most of the game is just following commands, not much skill is needed.  Then all of a sudden the final level increases the difficulty out of nowhere by 1000%.  It's very bizarre.  

This game is worth 5 dollars at most.

This game brings me comfort all out. I've only played the game for 2 hours but i have never felt at peace as i am playing Hades. I will certainly get the sequel soon enough, although i might even just keep replaying this game no matter what.

It teaches me that failure is okay, we can get better and move forward as long was we put the effort into the journey. It brings me comfort since im at the lowest point of my life, but as long as i put the effort in being better and moving forward, i can continue on with my journey even if i stumble.

I love how no matter how many times we die in the game, the relationships with the characters that we had are still there. Even if we fail, some of them teach us things or simply just pities us (Hades cough)

Again, this has to be my all time favorite game, thank you to the team that made this, i absolutely love the game, thank you.

Personally, I enjoy it but I enjoy most Space-themed content so I may not be the best judge. The story's good but could use more character and friendship development like previous games. Feels like Alien: Isolation and The Thing had a baby.

It's a pretty fun and relaxing game to waste time, and it hooks you. My main complaint is the game feeling the need to hand hold frequently, and stopping me from actually playing the game to hit spacebar repeatedly every other time I finish fishing to tell me about some event or new feature, it really gets old. I know this is a difficult thing to avoid in games but there are better ways of doing it, drip feeding new mechanics and mini games is easier on most people but it really has to be balanced with just letting the player play the game and leaving them alone. It's like Navi from OOT. I guess it's a good sign of the gameplay loop that I'm still playing it and I'm not gonna quit playing the game but it's souring and I may be done soon.
Definitely a few parts where they went for atmosphere over fun, but a quick little story that's worth a playthrough.

Felt like It Takes Two but worse. First off, the story is UNBELIEVABLY hoaky, like Creative Writing 101 student assignment tier. And the gameplay both fails to live up to It Takes Two and also fails to improve on any of its flaws. Most apparent and most unfortunate is that is zero reason to ever explore. There is nothing there, anywhere. Just go straight ahead, over and over. The actual *fun* moments are so few and few between, maybe every 30 minutes of play you get 5-10 minutes of decent platforming, 10+ minutes of excruciating story, and another 10 minutes of running around with very little going on. It's just not worth the time.
I loved this game and will definitely check out the developer's other stuff.

This game is never short on action. Although it is incredibly difficult, it never feels unfair or gets frustrating, since you are put right back into the action. The parkour segments were unlike anything I’ve ever played.

Fast-paced gameplay, solid shooting, plenty of weapon choices, great music, each level takes only about 3 minutes so its easy to pick up and put down, I also like the crass humor and the freakish artstyle.

It's a good game with some flaws. Way better than the first game and super ambitious, which you have to respect coming from a small dev team. The first half of the game is far stronger than the second; with the endgame area making Lost Izalith look good by comparison. 

Great graphics and fun combat, a very cool world to explore, but some questionable design choices here and there bring it down a little. Good news is that the devs are actively working on correcting issues and adding content at the moment. 

All in all, took me 50 hours to get 100% across 3 playthroughs (which is now easier thanks to farmable glimpses).

Something about the combat is off-putting after coming from silksong and Gris. It's really clunky and slow which leaves me feeling frustrated whenever there's a combat scene. Dunno ... I miss Gris. This just isn't hitting for me. 

Update. A few more hours in and still hate the combat. Can't wait for this to be over.

Parkour constitutes like 40% of the game time. It's not enjoyable.

Having said that, the other elements of the games: combat, animations, music, are all excellent. In fact an excellent piece of art. 

If you are fine with grinding parkour parts, definitely should buy this!

One of the best open-world games of all time, and maybe even the best.
I enjoyed every single moment I spent in this game. I absolutely hate puzzles, but Crimson Desert is so beautiful and enjoyable that I can easily ignore that.
I really love open-world games that give you a lot of things to do, and I'm very happy that Crimson Desert gives players so much freedom. You can explore, fight, complete different activities, and just enjoy the world however you want.
The only thing I wish this masterpiece had was romance. Apparently, romance might be added in an expansion, and if that really happens, this game will be almost perfect for me.
And finally, I'm really happy that Crimson Desert became so successful and proved those Metacritic critics wrong.

Besides the fact this game has no one playing it. My friend and I bought the game. We had a ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ blast. The bots do try to murder you if they are the killer. They do collect resources and hoard them sometimes. This game is fun to play with friends. A dead game is only dead until people revive it. Does it need some optimization? Yeah, a bit, there is a delay in when the game announces someone dies. A mic bug that's solved by leaving the lobby and coming back. Those are my biggest issues. However, I love the look of it cause it's like those old PS2 games honestly. I've seen worse graphics. This game is fun and we bought it on a sale. Major props to the Dev who kept putting out content and bug fixes when the game slowed down. Even put out a Halloween event. I hope it comes out this year too, cause I would like to play it with my friends.

No other game has hit the highs that this can deliver with friends, so many great game modes and maps, and the amount of fan service is just perfect. I will say though... that library mission... end me.

As a metroidavania lover and an artist, I can't recommendConstance enough! This game shines as a metroidvania with great and challenging platforming and rewarding exploration as you progress and gets new skills. All the art direction is amazing, great colors, charming character design and fluid animations! 

And as an artist who also struggled (and sometimes still do) with burnout, anxiety and depression, this is such a sensible and heartwarming way to approach this subject! 

Played both on PC and Steam Deck, strongly recommend it!!
